BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):

- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the basis of division first. 2) the tree from the top down. 3) each kind with its identifying feature and an example. 4) the borderline cases and exceptions. 5) the tree as recap.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.

  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.

  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

Video v4: Muscle कैसे काम करती है? Skeletal और smooth muscle
Goal: तुम muscle contraction का book-level क्रम, muscle classes, skeletal muscle की movement और posture में भूमिका तथा smooth muscle और peristalsis समझोगे।
Opening hook: हाथ तुम अपनी मर्ज़ी से चलाते हो, लेकिन खाना अंदर आगे कैसे बढ़ता है?
Story or analogy: Tube पर आगे बढ़ती दबाव की wave से peristalsis समझाएँगे; इसे केवल movement की analogy रखेंगे, microscopic mechanism नहीं।
Planned minutes: 7
Narration time (S2-01): 5.9-7.9 minutes, about 767-1027 spoken words (BIE counts 130 words a minute)
Prerequisites already taught in the prerequisite video (remind of one in at most 2 beats): Cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus and basic plant-cell parts; Chromosome sets, DNA copying and nuclear versus cell division; Body covering, cavity, lumen and gland duct; Diffusion, absorption and secretion; Strength, flexibility, elasticity and rigidity; Contraction, relaxation, fatigue and voluntary control; Root and shoot tips, nodes, internodes, leaf base and girth; Photosynthesis, food storage and root water–mineral uptake

  p005-i18#q1 | what | What are the cellular units of muscle tissue called? → The page calls them muscle cells or muscle fibres. | book
  p005-i18#q2 | where | Where are these muscle fibres found? → They are the cells composing muscle tissue. | book
  p005-i18#q3 | why | Why is distinguishing a muscle fibre from a connective tissue fibre important? → A muscle fibre is a cell, whereas the collagen and elastic fibres described above are extracellular protein structures. The same word 'fibre' refers to different kinds of biological components. | outside

  p005-i19#q1 | what | What general shape and size does the page assign to muscle fibres? → They are elongated and large sized. | book
  p005-i19#q2 | where | Where does this description apply? → It appears among the general characteristics of muscle tissue. | book
  p005-i19#q3 | how | How does an elongated cell shape relate to muscular action? → It allows contractile structures to be arranged along the cell's length so that shortening produces a directed pull. | outside
p005-i20 | 5 | list_point | structure | Contractile proteins are present in fibres.
  p005-i20#q1 | what | What special proteins occur in muscle fibres? → Contractile proteins, meaning proteins involved in the fibre's ability to generate force and contract. | outside
  p005-i20#q2 | where | Where are these proteins located according to the page? → Within the muscle fibres. | book
  p005-i20#q3 | how | How do contractile proteins enable muscular action? → Actin and myosin interact using energy from ATP. Their relative sliding can shorten the contractile apparatus and generate tension. | outside
p005-i21 | 5 | list_point | process | Contraction and relaxation.
  p005-i21#q1 | what | Which two activities characterise muscle tissue here? → Contraction is the active generation of muscle tension, which may shorten the muscle and produce a pull. Relaxation is the reduction of that active tension as activation subsides. These explain the two activities named on the page. | outside
  p005-i21#q2 | how | How do contraction and relaxation differ? → During contraction, muscle develops active tension and may shorten. During relaxation, activation and active tension decline, allowing the muscle to return towards a resting state as loads and other tissues act on it. | outside
  p005-i21#q3 | when | When does a muscle move from contraction towards relaxation? → It does so as the activating signal subsides and the conditions sustaining interaction of the contractile proteins are reduced. | outside
  p005-i21#q4 | why | Why are both activities needed for movement? → Movement requires controlled force as well as its reduction so that a body part can change direction or be repositioned by other forces and muscles. | outside

  p005-i22#q1 | which | Which types of muscle tissue are listed? → Skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle tissue. | book
  p005-i22#q2 | difference | How can a teacher initially distinguish these three types? → Skeletal muscle is generally associated with bones and voluntary movement; smooth muscle is found in many hollow organ walls and lacks striations; cardiac muscle forms the heart's muscular wall and is striated and involuntary. Details of smooth and cardiac muscle are not given on this page. | outside
  p005-i22#q3 | how | How should students use this list while studying the skeletal subsection? → Treat skeletal muscle as one member of a three-part classification and attach its listed features to that member rather than assuming those features describe all muscle tissue. | outside
p005-i24 | 5 | list_point | structure | Muscle fibres are elongated and cylindrical Unbranched
  p005-i24#q1 | what | What shape identifies skeletal muscle fibres on this page? → They are elongated, cylindrical and unbranched. | book
  p005-i24#q2 | where | Where can these features be seen on the page? → The lower-right illustration represents skeletal muscle fibres as separate elongated cylindrical units without branching. | book
  p005-i24#q3 | how | How should a student interpret 'unbranched'? → A fibre continues as one elongated cell rather than dividing into side branches; several neighbouring fibres should not be mistaken for branches of one cell. | outside
p005-i25 | 5 | list_point | structure | Attached to bones
  p005-i25#q1 | what | What attachment does the page state for skeletal muscle? → It is attached to bones. | book
  p005-i25#q2 | where | Where is an example of this association illustrated? → The lower-right illustration shows an arm muscle alongside the bones of a bent arm. | book
  p005-i25#q3 | how | How can attachment to bones produce movement? → Skeletal muscles commonly transmit tension through tendons to bones. The resulting pull can turn a bone about a joint. | outside
p005-i26 | 5 | list_point | structure | Each cell is multi-nucleated → many nuclei.
  p005-i26#q1 | what | What does multi-nucleated mean here? → A single skeletal muscle cell contains many nuclei; the arrow introduces the meaning of the term rather than a process. | book
  p005-i26#q2 | where | Where are the many nuclei located? → They are within each skeletal muscle cell, not merely distributed across a collection of separate cells. | book
  p005-i26#q3 | why | Why can one skeletal muscle fibre have many nuclei? → Skeletal muscle fibres develop through fusion of precursor cells, bringing multiple nuclei into the resulting long fibre. | outside
p005-i27 | 5 | list_point | structure | Striations are present → alternate dark and light bands.
  p005-i27#q1 | what | What are the striations described by the page? → They are alternating dark and light bands. The arrow explains the term 'striations'. | book
  p005-i27#q2 | where | Where are these striations present? → They are present in skeletal muscle fibres and are represented by repeated bands in the lower-right illustration. | book
  p005-i27#q3 | why | Why does skeletal muscle show alternating bands? → Its contractile filaments are arranged in repeating, aligned units with regions of different filament composition and overlap, creating a banded appearance under the microscope. | outside
  p005-i27#q4 | exception | Is the presence of striations alone enough to distinguish skeletal from every other muscle type? → No. Cardiac muscle also has striations, so identification should combine banding with features such as fibre shape, branching and nuclei. | outside
p005-i28 | 5 | list_point | facts_numbers | Easily fatigue
  p005-i28#q1 | what | What does the page state about skeletal muscle fatigue? → It lists 'Easily fatigue' as a characteristic. | book
  p005-i28#q2 | evidence | What evidence for this statement is supplied on the page? → The page gives the characteristic as a bullet point but provides no experiment, measurement or comparison of fatigue rates. | book
  p005-i28#q3 | how | How should fatigue be explained to a beginner? → Fatigue is a decline in the ability to sustain the required force during continued activity. It reflects several physiological factors, including changes in energy supply and muscle activation. | outside
  p005-i28#q4 | exception | Should 'easily fatigue' be applied equally to every skeletal muscle and activity? → No. Fatigue resistance varies with fibre type, training and the intensity and duration of activity. The book's bullet is a broad introductory simplification. | outside
p005-i29 | 5 | list_point | cause_effect | Helps in body movement.
  p005-i29#q1 | why | Why is skeletal muscle important for body movement? → Its contraction generates pulling force that can be transmitted to bones, producing movement at joints. | outside
  p005-i29#q2 | how | How does the arm illustration help explain this role? → It places muscle alongside the bones of a bent arm, illustrating the association between skeletal muscle and limb movement. | book
  p005-i29#q3 | how | How can a body part move back in the opposite direction? → Muscles commonly act in opposing groups: one produces a particular pull, while another can produce the opposite movement as their activation changes. | outside
p005-i30 | 5 | list_point | cause_effect | Maintains posture
  p005-i30#q1 | why | Why are skeletal muscles needed to maintain posture? → Gravity and other loads tend to change body position. Appropriate muscle tension supports body segments and stabilises joints. | outside
  p005-i30#q2 | how | How can muscles maintain posture without an obvious movement? → They can develop tension while their overall length changes little, balancing the forces that would otherwise move the body. | outside
  p005-i30#q3 | difference | How does this function differ from producing body movement? → Movement changes the position of body parts; posture maintenance helps preserve a position. Both depend on controlled muscle force. | outside
p005-i31 | 5 | list_point | definition | Other names: Skeleton muscle, Striated muscle and voluntary muscle.
  p005-i31#q1 | what | Which other names does the book give skeletal muscle? → It lists 'Skeleton muscle', 'Striated muscle' and 'voluntary muscle'. | book
  p005-i31#q2 | evidence | Which earlier features on this page explain the names associated with skeleton and striations? → Attachment to bones explains the skeletal association, while alternating dark and light bands explain the name striated muscle. | book
  p005-i31#q3 | why | Why is skeletal muscle called voluntary muscle? → Its activity can generally be initiated and controlled consciously, as when deliberately moving a limb. | outside
  p005-i31#q4 | exception | Does the name voluntary mean every skeletal muscle contraction requires conscious choice? → No. Skeletal muscles also participate in reflexes and automatic postural adjustments. 'Voluntary' describes their capacity for conscious control. | outside

There are no directional arrows or process stages.
  p005-i32#q1 | what | What two views does the skeletal muscle illustration combine? → A schematic view of muscle fibres and an anatomical example of an arm muscle associated with bones. | book
  p005-i32#q2 | which | Which written skeletal muscle characteristics are represented visually? → Elongated cylindrical unbranched fibres, banding, multiple nuclei and association with the skeleton. | book
  p005-i32#q3 | how | How does combining these views improve understanding? → The fibre view helps identify the tissue's cellular appearance, while the arm view connects that tissue to a familiar body location and movement role. | outside
  p005-i32#q4 | why | Why should the blue ovals and orange-red fibres be read as schematic features? → The colours make nuclei and fibres easy to distinguish. They are illustrative conventions rather than evidence that living nuclei or fibres have those exact colours. | outside
p005-i33 | 5 | diagram_label | figure | Skeletal Muscle — identifies the illustrated group of cylindrical, banded muscle fibres.
  p005-i33#q1 | what | What tissue does the label name? → Skeletal muscle. | book
  p005-i33#q2 | which | Which part of the illustration is directly identified by the label? → The group of elongated cylindrical fibres shown to the left of the arm drawing. | book
  p005-i33#q3 | how | How can the identification be supported beyond reading the label? → The drawing combines unbranched cylindrical fibres, repeated transverse bands and several nuclei, matching the skeletal muscle features listed in the text. | book
p006-i3 | 6 | list_point | structure | • Fibres are spindle shaped/fusiform i.e. pointed at ends/tapering ends.
  p006-i3#q1 | what | What does spindle shaped or fusiform mean? → The fibre tapers towards pointed ends. 'Spindle shaped' and 'fusiform' describe the same shape here. | book
  p006-i3#q2 | where | Where is this shape found in the muscle types on this page? → It describes the fibres of visceral or smooth muscle. | book
  p006-i3#q3 | how | How would a student recognise a fusiform fibre in a drawing? → Look for a wider middle that narrows towards both ends, rather than a fibre of approximately uniform width. | outside
p006-i4 | 6 | list_point | structure | • Single and centrally located nucleus in each cell.
  p006-i4#q1 | what | What is the number of nuclei stated for a smooth muscle cell? → Each cell has a single nucleus. | book
  p006-i4#q2 | where | Where is the nucleus located? → It lies centrally within the cell. | book
  p006-i4#q3 | how | How should nucleus number and nucleus position be recorded separately? → Number answers how many nuclei a cell contains; position answers where the nucleus lies. For smooth muscle here, the two observations are one nucleus and a central position. | outside
p006-i5 | 6 | list_point | structure | • Striations are absent.
  p006-i5#q1 | what | What feature is absent from smooth muscle fibres? → They lack striations, which is consistent with the page's alternative name 'Unstriated'. | book
  p006-i5#q2 | where | Where would striations be looked for? → They would be looked for as repeated bands across the muscle fibre under a microscope. | outside
  p006-i5#q3 | why | Why can smooth muscle contract despite lacking visible striations? → It contains contractile proteins, but these are not arranged in the regular repeating sarcomeres that produce the banded appearance of striated muscle. | outside
p006-i6 | 6 | list_point | structure | • Unbranched
  p006-i6#q1 | what | What does the page state about branching in smooth muscle? → Smooth muscle fibres are unbranched. | book
  p006-i6#q2 | where | Where does the branching description apply? → It applies to the shape of an individual fibre, rather than to the overall outline of an organ containing the tissue. | outside
  p006-i6#q3 | how | How does this help distinguish smooth muscle from cardiac muscle? → Smooth muscle fibres are unbranched, whereas the cardiac fibres described below are branched. | book
p006-i7 | 6 | list_point | facts_numbers | • Do not fatigue
  p006-i7#q1 | what | What fatigue characteristic does the book assign to smooth muscle? → The book states that smooth muscle fibres do not fatigue. | book
  p006-i7#q2 | evidence | What on this page supports teaching this as a smooth muscle characteristic? → It is explicitly listed under smooth muscle characteristics. The page provides no experimental evidence or measurements. | book
  p006-i7#q3 | how | How should this simplified statement be understood physiologically? → Smooth muscle is well suited to sustained activity and can maintain tension with relatively low energy use. p006-i8 | 6 | list_point | process | • Performs functions like peristalsis.
  p006-i8#q1 | what | Which function of smooth muscle is named here? → The page names peristalsis as a function performed by smooth muscle. | book
  p006-i8#q2 | how | How does peristalsis move material? → Coordinated waves of contraction and relaxation in the wall of a hollow organ move its contents along. In the digestive tract, contraction behind a portion of food and relaxation ahead help propel it forward. | outside
  p006-i8#q3 | when | When is digestive peristalsis used? → It operates as digestive contents are moved through the tract, without requiring a conscious decision for each movement. | outside
  p006-i8#q4 | why | Why must the contractions be coordinated? → A travelling pattern can propel contents along the tube; an isolated squeeze mainly changes the local shape or pressure. | outside
p006-i9 | 6 | paragraph | classification | Other names: Unstriated/Involuntary muscles
  p006-i9#q1 | which | Which other names are given for smooth muscle? → The page gives 'Unstriated' and 'Involuntary muscles'. Its heading also calls it visceral muscle. | book
  p006-i9#q2 | difference | What is the difference between the criteria expressed by unstriated and involuntary? → Unstriated describes the absence of visible bands; involuntary describes activity that is not ordinarily under conscious control. | outside
  p006-i9#q3 | why | Why should these names not be treated as interchangeable classification criteria? → Appearance and control are different properties. The page itself shows that cardiac muscle is striated while also being involuntary. | outside
p006-i10 | 6 | example | structure | Example: Stomach, Intestine, eye, blood vessel etc.
  p006-i10#q1 | what | What do the listed examples illustrate? → They illustrate structures in which smooth muscle occurs. | book
  p006-i10#q2 | where | Where does the page place smooth muscle? → The named examples are the stomach, intestine, eye and blood vessel. | book
  p006-i10#q3 | where | Where within these examples is the smooth muscle found? → It occurs in muscular parts of the stomach and intestinal walls, in the walls of many blood vessels, and in structures of the eye such as the iris and ciliary muscle. | outside
  p006-i10#q4 | how | How can one tissue type serve these different structures? → Its contraction has different effects according to its arrangement: it can move digestive contents, change vessel diameter, or alter pupil size and lens accommodation in the eye. | outside

frame.process: Muscle tissue consists of elongated cells containing contractile proteins.
frame.how: Read from tissue to fibre and then to proteins inside the fibre.
frame.when: Establish the cellular structure before explaining activity.
frame.conditions: Muscle fibre means a cell in this context.
frame.atmosphere: A tissue-to-cell schematic.

frame.process: Muscle generates active tension and subsequently relaxes.
frame.how: Activation enables contractile action; declining activation reduces active tension.
frame.when: Contraction precedes relaxation in the simplified teaching sequence.
frame.conditions: Force generation needs activation and energy; shortening is not obligatory.
frame.atmosphere: A deliberately moved limb.

frame.process: Muscle tissue is organised into three classes.
frame.how: Distinguish classes using location, cellular appearance and control.
frame.when: Introduce the tree before studying skeletal and smooth muscle.
frame.conditions: Traits of one class must not be generalised to all muscle.
frame.atmosphere: A three-branch classification tree.

frame.process: Skeletal muscle links cellular structure with attachment to bones.
frame.how: Move from bone association to fibre outline, bands and nuclei.
frame.when: Inspect structure before function.
frame.conditions: Multiple nuclei belong to a single cell; neighbouring fibres are not branches.
frame.atmosphere: An arm beside an enlarged skeletal fibre.

frame.process: The book characterises skeletal muscle as easily fatigued.
frame.how: Explain fatigue through declining ability to sustain force.
frame.when: During continued activity.
frame.conditions: Fatigue varies with muscle and activity; the book supplies no measurements.
frame.atmosphere: A familiar sustained muscle effort.

frame.process: Skeletal muscle produces movement and maintains posture.
frame.how: Muscle force either changes position or balances forces to preserve position.
frame.when: During movement and while holding a posture.
frame.conditions: Contraction need not produce visible shortening or motion.
frame.atmosphere: A moving arm followed by a supported body position.

frame.process: Alternative names describe skeletal association, banding and conscious control.
frame.how: Connect each name to its identifying property.
frame.when: After learning skeletal structure and function.
frame.conditions: Voluntary does not mean every contraction is consciously chosen.
frame.atmosphere: A student choosing to move a hand.

frame.process: The figure links skeletal fibres with an arm muscle.
frame.how: Read the left fibre group and label, then the bent arm at right.
frame.when: After the skeletal-muscle explanation.
frame.conditions: Colours are schematic; the image is not a process sequence.
frame.atmosphere: The described two-part Skeletal Muscle illustration.

frame.process: Smooth muscle has tapered unbranched cells with one central nucleus and no striations.
frame.how: Locate the tissue, inspect cell outline, then inspect its interior.
frame.when: Introduce smooth structure before peristalsis.
frame.conditions: Absence of bands does not imply absence of contractile proteins.
frame.atmosphere: Smooth cells associated with stomach, intestine, eye and blood vessels.

frame.process: The book describes smooth muscle as not fatiguing.
frame.how: Interpret this as suitability for sustained normal activity.
frame.when: During sustained organ activity.
frame.conditions: This is a broad fatigue-resistance statement, not unlimited performance.
frame.atmosphere: Repeated activity in internal organs.

frame.process: Peristalsis moves contents through a hollow organ.
frame.how: A travelling pattern of contraction behind and relaxation ahead propels contents.
frame.when: As digestive contents pass through the tract.
frame.conditions: Contractions must be coordinated rather than isolated squeezes.
frame.atmosphere: Food within an intestinal tube.

frame.process: Smooth muscle is also called visceral, Unstriated and Involuntary.
frame.how: Separate naming by location, appearance and control.
frame.when: After smooth structure and activity are understood.
frame.conditions: Appearance and voluntary control are independent criteria.
frame.atmosphere: A naming tree with separate criteria.

frame.how: Read cells and label at left, then the digestive illustration at right.
frame.when: After explaining smooth muscle and peristalsis.

beats.say: हाथ तुम अपनी मर्ज़ी से चलाते हो। लेकिन खाना अंदर आगे कैसे बढ़ता है? दोनों में muscle काम करती है, पर उसका type और control अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hand movement beside food moving through the digestive tract.

beats.say: पहले muscle tissue को खोलकर देखो। इसे बनाने वाली cells को muscle cells या muscle fibres कहते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Muscle tissue → muscle cell / muscle fibre.

beats.say: एक fibre पर आओ: यह elongated और large sized cell है। इसके अंदर contractile proteins मौजूद हैं।
beats.on_screen: Zoom from tissue to elongated cell and proteins inside.

beats.say: Contractile proteins force पैदा करने में काम आते हैं। लम्बी cell में उनका arrangement लम्बाई की दिशा में खिंचाव पैदा कर सकता है।
beats.on_screen: Long fibre with longitudinal force arrows.

beats.say: कई fibres की activity मिलकर पूरी muscle का खिंचाव बनाती है। यानी अंदर के proteins का काम tissue के काम से जुड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Protein action → fibre force → muscle force.

beats.say: चित्र के labels याद रखो: muscle tissue, लम्बी muscle fibre, और उसके अंदर contractile proteins।
beats.on_screen: Labelled tissue–cell–protein recap.

beats.say: इसका नतीजा है force बनाना और फिर उसे घटाना। Book इन activities को contraction और relaxation कहती है।
beats.on_screen: Contraction: active tension rises. Relaxation: active tension falls.

beats.say: यह काम fibre के अंदर होता है। इसे शुरू करने के लिए activating signal और energy चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Signal and energy entering a simplified muscle-fibre model.

beats.say: Activation पर contractile proteins force बनाते हैं; muscle छोटी हो सकती है। Activation घटने पर active tension घटती है: यही relaxation है।
beats.on_screen: Activation → force; reduced activation → reduced force.

beats.say: Force बने ही नहीं तो खिंचाव नहीं होगा। Force ठीक समय पर घटे नहीं, तो दूसरी movement में रुकावट आएगी।
beats.on_screen: Failed force generation versus force not reduced appropriately.

beats.say: पूरा क्रम देखो: activation, force बनना, फिर activation घटना और relaxation। छोटी होना contraction का अकेला मतलब नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Replay simplified contraction–relaxation sequence.

beats.say: Flow में याद करो: contraction में active tension बढ़ती है; relaxation में घटती है।
beats.on_screen: Contraction → active tension; relaxation → reduction.

beats.say: Muscles को अलग पहचानने में उनकी बनावट, जगह और control देखते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Classification criteria: structure, location, control.

beats.say: Book का tree muscle tissue से 3 branches बनाता है: Skeletal, Smooth और Cardiac।
beats.on_screen: Muscle tissue → Skeletal / Smooth / Cardiac.

beats.say: Skeletal को bones से, Smooth को intestine जैसे organs से जोड़ो। Cardiac heart की muscle है; उसे अगले video में पढ़ेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Bone and arm; intestine; heart.

beats.say: एक branch की features सब पर मत लगाना। हर muscle की cells skeletal जैसी नहीं होतीं।
beats.on_screen: Keep skeletal features within the skeletal branch.

beats.say: Tree वापस देखो: Skeletal, Smooth, Cardiac। अब पहली branch खोलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight Skeletal branch.

beats.say: Skeletal muscle bones से attached होती है। Book में मुड़ी हुई arm के bones के साथ muscle दिखाई गई है।
beats.on_screen: Bent arm showing muscle associated with bones.

beats.say: बाहर से fibre elongated, cylindrical और unbranched है। अंदर alternate dark और light bands हैं; एक cell में कई nuclei हैं।
beats.on_screen: Outline → alternating bands → multiple nuclei in one fibre.

beats.say: Bone से attachment खिंचाव को movement से जोड़ती है। Bands अंदर contractile structures के नियमित arrangement से दिखते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Attachment transmits pull; regular internal arrangement produces banding.

beats.say: Fibres मिलकर force बनाती हैं और bones तक पहुँचाती हैं। Unbranched का मतलब एक fibre की side branches नहीं; पास की fibres अलग cells हैं।
beats.on_screen: Separate parallel fibres transmitting collective force toward a bone.

beats.say: Labels जोड़ो: cylindrical, unbranched, multi-nucleated और striations। Fibre drawing में यही पहचान मिलेगी।
beats.on_screen: Labelled skeletal fibre recap.

beats.say: Skeletal muscle के लिए book कहती है: Easily fatigue। यानी लगातार काम में required force बनाए रखने की क्षमता घट सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Easily fatigue → declining ability to sustain required force.

beats.say: हाथ देर तक उठाए रखने की मेहनत सोचो। यहाँ कोई numerical fatigue rate नहीं दी गई है।
beats.on_screen: Sustained raised arm; no numerical scale.

beats.say: यह book का characteristic है, page पर किसी experiment या measurement का result नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Book statement; no experimental data supplied.

beats.say: इसे broad feature समझो। हर skeletal muscle बराबर जल्दी नहीं थकती; activity और training से फर्क पड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Fatigue varies with muscle and activity; no formula supplied.

beats.say: Skeletal muscle के 2 काम देखो: body movement और posture बनाए रखना।
beats.on_screen: Moving arm versus maintaining body position.

beats.say: दोनों के पीछे muscle force है। फर्क यह कि position बदलनी है या बचाए रखनी है।
beats.on_screen: Same muscle force → change position / preserve position.

beats.say: Contraction का pull bones तक पहुँचकर joint पर movement कराता है। Posture में tension, gravity जैसे forces को balance करती है।
beats.on_screen: Pull turns bone at joint; balanced forces preserve posture.

beats.say: Book की bent arm में bones के साथ muscle बनी है। यही drawing muscle और limb movement का रिश्ता दिखाती है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight muscle–bone association in the arm illustration.

beats.say: Force का मतलब हमेशा दिखती movement नहीं। Posture में muscle की overall length बहुत कम बदलकर भी tension बनी रह सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Stable position with active muscle tension.

beats.say: Chain याद रखो: muscle force, फिर position बदलना या position बनाए रखना।
beats.on_screen: Muscle force → movement / posture.

beats.say: तुम अपनी मर्ज़ी से हाथ उठाते हो। इसी control से voluntary muscle नाम समझो।
beats.on_screen: Deliberate hand movement.

beats.say: Book के other names हैं Skeleton muscle, Striated muscle और voluntary muscle। Bones से रिश्ता पहला नाम, bands दूसरा नाम समझाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Skeleton muscle: bones; Striated muscle: bands; voluntary muscle: control.

beats.say: Voluntary का मतलब हर contraction सोचकर नहीं होता। Reflexes और automatic posture adjustments भी skeletal muscles कर सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Capacity for conscious control ≠ every contraction consciously chosen.

beats.say: अब figure में इन्हीं नामों के पीछे वाली features पहचानो।
beats.on_screen: Transition from names to skeletal figure.

beats.say: यह figure 2 views जोड़ती है: fibres की बनावट और arm में muscle की जगह।
beats.on_screen: Complete two-part skeletal-muscle illustration.

beats.say: बाएँ orange-red cylinders में bands और कई blue nuclei देखो। नीचे Skeletal Muscle label इसी group का है; दाएँ bent arm है।
beats.on_screen: Left fibres → bands → nuclei → Skeletal Muscle label → right arm.

beats.say: पहचान का मेल है: unbranched cylinders, bands और कई nuclei। Colours केवल समझाने के लिए हैं।
beats.on_screen: Identification checklist; schematic-colour notice.

beats.say: इस तरह cell की पहचान bones से जुड़ी muscle के movement वाले काम से जुड़ गई।
beats.on_screen: Fibre appearance linked to anatomical arm example.

beats.say: अब Smooth या visceral muscle। Book के examples हैं Stomach, Intestine, eye और blood vessel।
beats.on_screen: Smooth muscle associated with four named locations.

beats.say: बाहर से fibre spindle shaped या fusiform है: बीच चौड़ा, दोनों ends taper होते हैं; branching नहीं। अंदर 1 centrally located nucleus है और striations absent हैं।
beats.on_screen: Outline first, then one central nucleus and absence of bands.

beats.say: Bands नहीं हैं, फिर भी contraction होता है। Contractile proteins हैं, बस उनका arrangement skeletal muscle जैसी नियमित bands नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: No visible striations does not mean no contractile proteins.

beats.say: Organ की wall में cells मिलकर काम करती हैं। Intestine में उनकी coordinated activity contents आगे बढ़ा सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Multiple smooth cells acting in an intestinal wall.

beats.say: Labels पढ़ो: tapered ends, unbranched, 1 central nucleus, no striations। Cardiac से branching का फर्क भी याद रखो: वहाँ fibres branched हैं।
beats.on_screen: Labelled smooth cell; brief smooth-unbranched/card iac-branched contrast.

beats.say: Smooth muscle के लिए book लिखती है: Do not fatigue।
beats.on_screen: Smooth muscle: Do not fatigue.

beats.say: इसे skeletal के Easily fatigue के सामने रखो। कोई numerical comparison book में नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Qualitative fatigue comparison, without numerical rates.

beats.say: यह smooth muscle की listed characteristic है; page पर experiment या measurement नहीं दिया है।
beats.on_screen: Source: book characteristic, not measured data.

beats.say: मतलब normal conditions में sustained activity के लिए fatigue resistance है। हर condition में unlimited काम करना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Fatigue resistance under normal conditions; no formula supplied.

beats.say: Book इसका function peristalsis बताती है। इसमें tube के contents आगे बढ़ते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Peristalsis → forward movement of digestive contents.

beats.say: Intestine को hollow tube सोचो: अंदर खाना, wall में smooth muscle। यह movement हर बार तुम्हारे सोचने पर निर्भर नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Food within lumen; smooth muscle in wall.

beats.say: खाने के पीछे contraction और आगे relaxation होता है। यह pattern आगे चलता है, जिससे खाना आगे बढ़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Contraction behind contents; relaxation ahead; travelling wave.

beats.say: केवल एक जगह squeeze करने से local pressure बदल सकता है। आगे बढ़ाने के लिए contractions का coordination चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Isolated squeeze contrasted with coordinated travelling wave.

beats.say: नरम tube पर आगे चलती दबाव की wave सोचो। यह movement की analogy है, microscopic mechanism नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Soft-tube travelling-pressure analogy, explicitly labelled analogy.

beats.say: Flow है: पीछे contraction, आगे relaxation, travelling wave, contents आगे।
beats.on_screen: Four-link peristalsis flow.

beats.say: अब naming के आधार अलग करो: appearance और control अलग बातें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Separate criteria: appearance / control.

beats.say: Smooth muscle को heading में visceral और other names में Unstriated तथा Involuntary muscles कहा है।
beats.on_screen: Smooth / visceral → Unstriated; Involuntary muscles.

beats.say: Intestine में bands नहीं: Unstriated। उसकी activity आम तौर पर मर्ज़ी से नहीं चलाते: Involuntary।
beats.on_screen: Intestinal smooth muscle: no bands; not ordinarily consciously controlled.

beats.say: दोनों criteria मिलाना मत। Cardiac muscle striated होकर भी involuntary है।
beats.on_screen: Cardiac: striated + involuntary.

beats.say: Naming tree में Unstriated appearance बताता है; Involuntary control बताता है।
beats.on_screen: Recap tree with separate appearance and control branches.

beats.say: Smooth muscle figure cells को intestine से जोड़ती है। यह tissue और organ का रिश्ता है।
beats.on_screen: Full boxed smooth-cell and intestinal illustration.

beats.say: बाएँ orange tapered cells और blue nuclei देखो; bands नहीं हैं। नीचे Smooth Muscle label उन्हीं cells का है; दाएँ coiled intestine दिखती है।
beats.on_screen: Cells → nuclei → absent bands → label → coiled intestine inside large-intestine outline.

beats.say: Tapered shape और absent bands label को सही ठहराते हैं। Figure में peristalsis के stages या connecting arrows नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Identification cues highlighted; no process arrows added to source figure.

beats.say: Text से जोड़ो: यही smooth tissue intestine में मिलता है और peristalsis में काम करता है।
beats.on_screen: Smooth-cell appearance → intestinal location → named function.

frame.process: Muscle tissue consists of elongated cells containing contractile proteins.

frame.when: During continued activity.

frame.atmosphere: A familiar sustained muscle effort.

frame.process: Skeletal muscle produces movement and maintains posture.

notes.about: This review evaluates the script for video v4 covering muscle tissue basics, contraction, skeletal muscle, and smooth muscle with peristalsis.
key_questions: Are all 25 required items and their teacher questions properly answered?
Does the script stay within the word-count/time budget while maintaining teaching depth for UPSC/PCS aspirants?
Are content-type patterns and basis labels (book vs. outside) accurately applied?

decisions.decision: Fail the script due to unaddressed teacher questions across multiple parts.
decisions.reason: Questions such as p005-i18#q3 (muscle fibre vs connective tissue fibre), p005-i20#q3 (actin/myosin/ATP), p005-i26#q3 (fusion of precursor cells), p005-i27#q4 (cardiac also striated), p005-i29#q3 (opposing muscle groups), and p006-i10#q3/q4 (specific roles in eye, vessels, gut) are completely omitted, which violates S2-02 and G-02.

decisions.decision: Flag word count as minor/context for why questions were dropped.
decisions.reason: The script is ~730 words (slightly below the 767–1027 word target for 5.9–7.9 minutes), so there is ample room (~250 words) to include all the missing teacher questions without exceeding the time limit.

problems.problem: Two important teacher questions in c14.1 are completely omitted: p005-i18#q3 (distinguishing a cellular muscle fibre from an extracellular connective tissue fibre like collagen/elastin) and p005-i20#q3 (how actin and myosin interact using ATP to slide and generate tension).
problems.fix: Add explanations in c14.1 (marked as 'outside' or 'mixed') clarifying that a muscle fibre is a whole cell unlike extracellular collagen fibres, and briefly naming actin, myosin, and ATP sliding interaction.

problems.problem: Teacher question p005-i22#q2 is not listed in 'answers' and is only partially covered: b15 mentions locations (bones, organs, heart) but omits the initial distinguishing features required by the question (voluntary vs involuntary, striated vs unstriated).
problems.fix: Update b15 to briefly state the initial distinction across the three types (skeletal: bones/voluntary; smooth: hollow organs/unstriated; cardiac: heart/striated and involuntary) and claim p005-i22#q2.

problems.problem: Four teacher questions in c15.1 are omitted: p005-i25#q3 (transmitting tension via tendons to turn a bone about a joint), p005-i26#q3 (why a skeletal muscle cell is multi-nucleated: fusion of precursor cells), and p005-i27#q4 (the 'exception' question required by c15.1's card: striations alone cannot identify skeletal muscle because cardiac muscle is also striated).
problems.fix: Incorporate tendon transmission at a joint (p005-i25#q3), precursor cell fusion for multiple nuclei (p005-i26#q3), and the exception that cardiac muscle also has striations (p005-i27#q4) into the beats of c15.1.

problems.problem: Teacher question p005-i29#q3 (how a body part moves back in the opposite direction via opposing muscle groups) is completely missing from c15.3.
problems.fix: Add a sentence in c15.3 explaining that muscles work in opposing pairs/groups to pull a bone back in the opposite direction, and claim p005-i29#q3.

problems.problem: Several teacher questions in c16.1 are omitted: p006-i3#q3 (how to recognise fusiform vs uniform width in a drawing), p006-i4#q3 (distinguishing nucleus number from nucleus position), p006-i5#q2 (where striations are looked for—under a microscope across the fibre), p006-i6#q2 (branching applies to the individual fibre, not the organ outline), and p006-i10#q3 & p006-i10#q4 (where smooth muscle lies inside the stomach/intestine walls, blood vessel walls, and eye iris/ciliary muscle, and how its contraction serves each).
problems.fix: Expand the beats in c16.1 to explicitly address how smooth muscle works in blood vessels (changing diameter) and the eye (iris/ciliary muscle), as well as the observational details for fusiform shape, nucleus number vs position, microscopic bands, and fibre vs organ branching.

problems.problem: The spoken narration across all beats is approximately 725 words (~5.6 minutes at 130 wpm), which falls slightly short of the S2-01 target window of 5.9–7.9 minutes (767–1027 words).
problems.fix: Adding the missing explanations from the omitted teacher questions above will naturally bring the word count to around 850–900 words, right in the middle of the target range.

frame.process: Muscle tissue consists of elongated cells containing contractile proteins.
frame.how: Read from tissue to fibre and then to proteins inside the fibre.
frame.when: Establish the cellular structure before explaining activity.
frame.conditions: Muscle fibre means a cell in this context.
frame.atmosphere: A tissue-to-cell schematic.

frame.process: Muscle generates active tension and subsequently relaxes.
frame.how: Activation enables contractile action; declining activation reduces active tension.
frame.when: Contraction precedes relaxation in the simplified teaching sequence.
frame.conditions: Force generation needs activation and energy; shortening is not obligatory.
frame.atmosphere: A deliberately moved limb.

frame.process: Muscle tissue is organised into three classes.
frame.how: Distinguish classes using location, cellular appearance and control.
frame.when: Introduce the tree before studying skeletal and smooth muscle.
frame.conditions: Traits of one class must not be generalised to all muscle.
frame.atmosphere: A three-branch classification tree.

frame.process: Skeletal muscle links cellular structure with attachment to bones.
frame.how: Move from bone association to fibre outline, bands and nuclei.
frame.when: Inspect structure before function.
frame.conditions: Multiple nuclei belong to a single cell; neighbouring fibres are not branches.
frame.atmosphere: An arm beside an enlarged skeletal fibre.

frame.process: The book characterises skeletal muscle as easily fatigued.
frame.how: Explain fatigue through declining ability to sustain force.
frame.when: During continued activity.
frame.conditions: Fatigue varies with muscle and activity; the book supplies no measurements.
frame.atmosphere: A familiar sustained muscle effort.

frame.process: Skeletal muscle produces movement and maintains posture.
frame.how: Muscle force either changes position or balances forces to preserve position.
frame.when: During movement and while holding a posture.
frame.conditions: Contraction need not produce visible shortening or motion.
frame.atmosphere: A moving arm followed by a supported body position.

frame.process: Alternative names describe skeletal association, banding and conscious control.
frame.how: Connect each name to its identifying property.
frame.when: After learning skeletal structure and function.
frame.conditions: Voluntary does not mean every contraction is consciously chosen.
frame.atmosphere: A student choosing to move a hand.

frame.process: The figure links skeletal fibres with an arm muscle.
frame.how: Read the left fibre group and label, then the bent arm at right.
frame.when: After the skeletal-muscle explanation.
frame.conditions: Colours are schematic; the image is not a process sequence.
frame.atmosphere: The described two-part Skeletal Muscle illustration.

frame.process: Smooth muscle has tapered unbranched cells with one central nucleus and no striations.
frame.how: Locate the tissue, inspect cell outline, then inspect its interior.
frame.when: Introduce smooth structure before peristalsis.
frame.conditions: Absence of bands does not imply absence of contractile proteins.
frame.atmosphere: Smooth cells associated with stomach, intestine, eye and blood vessels.

frame.process: The book describes smooth muscle as not fatiguing.
frame.how: Interpret this as suitability for sustained normal activity.
frame.when: During sustained organ activity.
frame.conditions: This is a broad fatigue-resistance statement, not unlimited performance.
frame.atmosphere: Repeated activity in internal organs.

frame.process: Peristalsis moves contents through a hollow organ.
frame.how: A travelling pattern of contraction behind and relaxation ahead propels contents.
frame.when: As digestive contents pass through the tract.
frame.conditions: Contractions must be coordinated rather than isolated squeezes.
frame.atmosphere: Food within an intestinal tube.

frame.process: Smooth muscle is also called visceral, Unstriated and Involuntary.
frame.how: Separate naming by location, appearance and control.
frame.when: After smooth structure and activity are understood.
frame.conditions: Appearance and voluntary control are independent criteria.
frame.atmosphere: A naming tree with separate criteria.

frame.process: The figure associates smooth cells with the intestine.
frame.how: Read cells and label at left, then the digestive illustration at right.
frame.when: After explaining smooth muscle and peristalsis.
frame.conditions: The side-by-side views show association, not stages of peristalsis.
frame.atmosphere: The described boxed Smooth Muscle illustration.

beats.say: हाथ तुम खुद चलाते हो। खाना अंदर कैसे बढ़ता है? दोनों में अलग muscle types काम करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hand movement beside digestive movement.

beats.say: Muscle tissue बनाने वाली cells को muscle cells या muscle fibres कहते हैं। यहाँ fibre पूरी cell है; connective tissue की collagen और elastic fibres cells के बाहर की protein structures हैं।
beats.on_screen: Contrast: muscle fibre = whole cell; collagen/elastic fibres = extracellular protein structures.

beats.say: एक fibre पर आओ: यह elongated और large sized cell है। इसके अंदर contractile proteins मौजूद हैं।
beats.on_screen: Zoom from tissue to elongated cell and proteins inside.

beats.say: Contractile proteins में actin और myosin, ATP की energy से interact करते हैं। उनके relative sliding से force बनती है और contractile arrangement छोटा हो सकता है। लम्बी cell में यह arrangement लम्बाई की दिशा में खिंचाव देता है।
beats.on_screen: Simplified actin–myosin relative sliding powered by ATP; force along the fibre.

beats.say: Fibres मिलकर पूरी muscle का खिंचाव बनाती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Protein action → fibre force → muscle force.

beats.say: Labels देखो: tissue, elongated fibre, अंदर contractile proteins।
beats.on_screen: Labelled tissue–cell–protein recap.

beats.say: इसका नतीजा है force बनाना और फिर उसे घटाना। Book इन activities को contraction और relaxation कहती है।
beats.on_screen: Contraction: active tension rises. Relaxation: active tension falls.

beats.say: यह काम fibre के अंदर होता है। इसे शुरू करने के लिए activating signal और energy चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Signal and energy entering a simplified muscle-fibre model.

beats.say: Activation पर contractile proteins force बनाते हैं; muscle छोटी हो सकती है। Activation घटने पर active tension घटती है: यही relaxation है।
beats.on_screen: Activation → force; reduced activation → reduced force.

beats.say: Force न बने तो खिंचाव नहीं; न घटे तो अगली movement में रुकावट।
beats.on_screen: Failure to generate force versus failure to reduce force.

beats.say: Activation, force, फिर activation घटना और relaxation। Contraction में छोटी होना ज़रूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Replay simplified contraction–relaxation sequence.

beats.say: Contraction: active tension बढ़ती है; relaxation: घटती है।
beats.on_screen: Contraction → increased active tension; relaxation → reduction.

beats.say: Muscles को अलग पहचानने में उनकी बनावट, जगह और control देखते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Classification criteria: structure, location, control.

beats.say: Book का tree muscle tissue से 3 branches बनाता है: Skeletal, Smooth और Cardiac।
beats.on_screen: Muscle tissue → Skeletal / Smooth / Cardiac.

beats.say: Skeletal: bones से जुड़ी, आम तौर पर voluntary। Smooth: intestine जैसे hollow organs में, unstriated। Cardiac: heart में, striated लेकिन involuntary।
beats.on_screen: Three branches with location, appearance and control distinguished.

beats.say: Skeletal की features हर muscle पर मत लगाना।
beats.on_screen: Keep skeletal features within the skeletal branch.

beats.say: 3 branches: Skeletal, Smooth, Cardiac। पहले Skeletal।
beats.on_screen: Three-branch tree; highlight Skeletal.

beats.say: Skeletal muscle bones से attached होती है। Book में मुड़ी हुई arm के bones के साथ muscle दिखाई गई है।
beats.on_screen: Bent arm showing muscle associated with bones.

beats.say: बाहर से fibre elongated, cylindrical और unbranched है। अंदर alternate dark और light bands हैं; एक cell में कई nuclei हैं।
beats.on_screen: Outline → alternating bands → multiple nuclei in one fibre.

beats.say: Muscle का tension आम तौर पर tendons से bone तक पहुँचकर उसे joint पर घुमाता है। Precursor cells के fusion से बनी skeletal fibre में कई nuclei आते हैं। Contractile structures का repeating arrangement dark और light bands बनाता है।
beats.on_screen: Tendon transmits pull to bone at joint; precursor-cell fusion explains multiple nuclei; repeating arrangement explains bands.

beats.say: Fibres मिलकर force बनाती हैं और bones तक पहुँचाती हैं। Unbranched का मतलब एक fibre की side branches नहीं; पास की fibres अलग cells हैं।
beats.on_screen: Separate parallel fibres transmitting collective force toward a bone.

beats.say: Figure में cylindrical, unbranched fibre, कई nuclei और striations पहचानो। केवल bands काफी नहीं: Cardiac में भी striations हैं। इसलिए features को मिलाकर पहचानना है।
beats.on_screen: Labelled skeletal fibre; striations alone are not diagnostic because cardiac muscle is also striated.

beats.say: Skeletal muscle के लिए book कहती है: Easily fatigue। यानी लगातार काम में required force बनाए रखने की क्षमता घट सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Easily fatigue → declining ability to sustain required force.

beats.say: देर तक हाथ उठाए रखने की मेहनत सोचो; numerical fatigue rate नहीं दी है।
beats.on_screen: Sustained raised arm; no numerical scale.

beats.say: यह book का characteristic है; experiment या measurement नहीं दिया।
beats.on_screen: Book statement; no experimental data supplied.

beats.say: इसे broad feature समझो। हर skeletal muscle बराबर जल्दी नहीं थकती; activity और training से फर्क पड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Fatigue varies with muscle and activity; no formula supplied.

beats.say: यह qualitative fact है, formula नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Qualitative characteristic; no formula supplied.

beats.say: Skeletal muscle के 2 काम देखो: body movement और posture बनाए रखना।
beats.on_screen: Moving arm versus maintaining body position.

beats.say: Muscle force position बदलती है या बनाए रखती है।
beats.on_screen: Muscle force → change position / preserve position.

beats.say: Contraction का pull bones को joint पर चलाता है। वापस उलटी दिशा में movement के लिए opposing muscle group खींच सकता है। Posture में muscle tension, gravity जैसे forces को balance करती है।
beats.on_screen: Opposing muscle groups produce opposite movements; balanced muscle force maintains posture.

beats.say: Book की bent arm में muscle–bone association movement का रिश्ता दिखाती है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight muscle and bones in the bent-arm illustration.

beats.say: Force का मतलब हमेशा दिखती movement नहीं। Posture में muscle की overall length बहुत कम बदलकर भी tension बनी रह सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Stable position with active muscle tension.

beats.say: Muscle force से movement या posture।
beats.on_screen: Muscle force → movement / posture.

beats.say: खुद हाथ उठाना voluntary control का example है।
beats.on_screen: Deliberate hand movement.

beats.say: Book के other names हैं Skeleton muscle, Striated muscle और voluntary muscle। Bones से रिश्ता पहला नाम, bands दूसरा नाम समझाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Skeleton muscle: bones; Striated muscle: bands; voluntary muscle: control.

beats.say: Voluntary का मतलब हर contraction सोचकर नहीं होता। Reflexes और automatic posture adjustments भी skeletal muscles कर सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Capacity for conscious control ≠ every contraction consciously chosen.

beats.say: अब figure में इन्हीं features को पहचानो।
beats.on_screen: Names linked to skeletal figure features.

beats.say: यह figure 2 views जोड़ती है: fibres की बनावट और arm में muscle की जगह।
beats.on_screen: Complete two-part skeletal-muscle illustration.

beats.say: बाएँ orange-red cylinders में bands और कई blue nuclei देखो। नीचे Skeletal Muscle label इसी group का है; दाएँ bent arm है।
beats.on_screen: Left fibres → bands → nuclei → Skeletal Muscle label → right arm.

beats.say: पहचान का मेल है: unbranched cylinders, bands और कई nuclei। Colours केवल समझाने के लिए हैं।
beats.on_screen: Identification checklist; schematic-colour notice.

beats.say: Cell की बनावट arm में उसकी जगह और movement से जुड़ी।
beats.on_screen: Fibre appearance linked to arm location and function.

beats.say: अब Smooth या visceral muscle। Book के examples हैं Stomach, Intestine, eye और blood vessel।
beats.on_screen: Smooth muscle associated with four named locations.

beats.say: Smooth fibre spindle shaped या fusiform है: बीच चौड़ा, दोनों ends taper होते हैं; width बराबर नहीं रहती। यह unbranched है। Branching एक fibre की देखनी है, पूरे organ के outline की नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Trace one fibre: wider middle, tapering ends, no side branches; contrast with a uniform-width cylinder.

beats.say: अंदर nucleus का number 1 है और position central है: कितने और कहाँ, अलग बातें हैं। Microscope में fibre के आर-पार repeated bands खोजते हैं; smooth muscle में ये striations absent हैं।
beats.on_screen: One nucleus: number; central: position. Microscopic view shows no repeated transverse bands.

beats.say: Bands absent हैं, contractile proteins नहीं। उनका arrangement skeletal जैसी repeating bands नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Contractile proteins remain present despite absent striations.

beats.say: Stomach और Intestine की walls में smooth cells मिलकर contents चलाती हैं। कई blood vessels की walls में contraction diameter बदलता है। Eye में iris की smooth muscle pupil size और ciliary muscle lens की focusing बदलती है।
beats.on_screen: Location → effect: digestive walls → contents movement; vessel walls → diameter; iris → pupil size; ciliary muscle → lens accommodation.

beats.say: Labels पढ़ो: tapered ends, unbranched, 1 central nucleus, no striations। Cardiac से branching का फर्क भी याद रखो: वहाँ fibres branched हैं।
beats.on_screen: Labelled smooth cell; brief smooth-unbranched/card iac-branched contrast.

beats.say: Smooth muscle के लिए book लिखती है: Do not fatigue।
beats.on_screen: Smooth muscle: Do not fatigue.

beats.say: Skeletal: Easily fatigue; Smooth: Do not fatigue। Numerical comparison नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Qualitative fatigue comparison only.

beats.say: यह listed characteristic है; experiment या measurement नहीं दिया।
beats.on_screen: Book characteristic, not measured data.

beats.say: मतलब normal conditions में sustained activity के लिए fatigue resistance है। हर condition में unlimited काम करना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Fatigue resistance under normal conditions; no formula supplied.

beats.say: यह भी qualitative fact है, formula नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Qualitative characteristic; no formula supplied.

beats.say: Book इसका function peristalsis बताती है। इसमें tube के contents आगे बढ़ते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Peristalsis → forward movement of digestive contents.

beats.say: Intestine को hollow tube सोचो: अंदर खाना, wall में smooth muscle। यह movement हर बार तुम्हारे सोचने पर निर्भर नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Food within lumen; smooth muscle in wall.

beats.say: खाने के पीछे contraction और आगे relaxation होता है। यह pattern आगे चलता है, जिससे खाना आगे बढ़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Contraction behind contents; relaxation ahead; travelling wave.

beats.say: केवल एक जगह squeeze करने से local pressure बदल सकता है। आगे बढ़ाने के लिए contractions का coordination चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Isolated squeeze contrasted with coordinated travelling wave.

beats.say: पूरा क्रम tube पर आगे चलती दबाव की wave जैसा सोचो; यह movement की analogy है।
beats.on_screen: Replay contraction behind, relaxation ahead and forward movement; soft-tube analogy, not microscopic mechanism.

beats.say: Flow है: पीछे contraction, आगे relaxation, travelling wave, contents आगे।
beats.on_screen: Four-link peristalsis flow.

beats.say: अब naming के आधार अलग करो: appearance और control अलग बातें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Separate criteria: appearance / control.

beats.say: Smooth muscle को heading में visceral और other names में Unstriated तथा Involuntary muscles कहा है।
beats.on_screen: Smooth / visceral → Unstriated; Involuntary muscles.

beats.say: Intestine में bands absent: Unstriated। Activity आम तौर पर conscious control में नहीं: Involuntary।
beats.on_screen: Intestinal smooth muscle: appearance versus control.

beats.say: दोनों criteria मिलाना मत। Cardiac muscle striated होकर भी involuntary है।
beats.on_screen: Cardiac: striated + involuntary.

beats.say: Unstriated appearance है; Involuntary control है।
beats.on_screen: Separate appearance and control branches.

beats.say: Smooth muscle figure cells को intestine से जोड़ती है। यह tissue और organ का रिश्ता है।
beats.on_screen: Full boxed smooth-cell and intestinal illustration.

beats.say: बाएँ orange tapered cells और blue nuclei देखो; bands नहीं हैं। नीचे Smooth Muscle label उन्हीं cells का है; दाएँ coiled intestine दिखती है।
beats.on_screen: Cells → nuclei → absent bands → label → coiled intestine inside large-intestine outline.

beats.say: Tapered cells और absent bands से label की पहचान पक्की होती है। यह peristalsis के stages नहीं दिखाता; connecting arrows भी नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight identification cues; distinguish tissue–organ association from a process sequence.

beats.say: Text से जोड़ो: यही smooth tissue intestine में मिलता है और peristalsis में काम करता है।
beats.on_screen: Smooth-cell appearance → intestinal location → named function.
